newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-INTER, BARCELONA FAIL TO AGREE RONALDO FEE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER, BARCELONA FAIL TO AGREE RONALDO FEE.

text.p: Internazionale Milan and Barcelona failed to agree a transfer fee for Brazilian striker Ronaldo on Tuesday, a FIFA spokesman said.
The Italian and Spanish clubs failure to agree the player's move from Barcelona to Inter means the matter must now be settled by the world soccer body.
FIFA will on Wednesday propose the amount that Inter should pay for the recent transfer of Ronaldo, the world's most expensive player.

If the clubs don't agree a deal on the basis of FIFA's proposal by July 31, a special commission will impose a fee by early September, the spokesman added. He declined to speculate on the likely size of the fee.
FIFA ruled this month that 20-year-old Ronaldo was free of contractual obligations with Barcelona and could join Inter, pending final agreement on the fee.
After that ruling, Ronaldo joined Inter briefly on Sunday for a friendly match in Milan against English champions Manchester United.
On July 22 FIFA's Players Status Committee found that Ronaldo had validly bought out his employment contract with Barcelona for 4.0 billion pesetas ($25.8 million).
This payment, however, was not related to any additional transfer fee between the two clubs.
At that time FIFA said it would impose a binding amount if the clubs could not agree one.
